implementation_statement: Enterprise access control policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.5 (P06) apply to OT. STD-02.4 (OT access) covers DCS roles, SIS engineering access, remote access through the gateway, and local panel HMIs. Procedures PRC-02.6 and PRC-02.7 cover PLT-01 OT provisioning and break-glass access.

Workforce accounts for the gateway and OT DMZ come from identity governance. DCS, batch, historian, and SIS accounts are local to the OT directory and are provisioned by PLT-01 controls engineering from an approved request; about 412 OT user accounts. Gaps: 3 integrator accounts on the remote access gateway were shared by several integrator staff (POAM-005), and 3 of 25 sampled leavers still had enabled DCS accounts (POAM-023).
evidence: OT directory export 2026-08-11; gateway account list; P07 AC-2 results

implementation_statement: Identity governance automates joiner, mover, and leaver events for IT and gateway accounts. OT directory accounts are changed by a ticket generated from the HR leaver feed, but the change itself is manual (POAM-023).
evidence: Identity governance workflow; OT leaver tickets

implementation_statement: The DCS enforces five role levels (view, operator, supervisor, engineer, administrator) per plant area. The batch system separates recipe authoring from recipe approval. SIS logic solvers accept program changes only with the keyswitch in program, and keys are held by the Controls Engineering Manager.
evidence: DCS security configuration export; SIS key log

implementation_statement: Information flows follow the OT reference architecture (STD-01.2 annex A): ERP production orders reach the batch system only through the order relay in the OT DMZ; historian data leaves only through the one-way replication path to Cloud provider A; no direct path exists from the business network to the control network.
evidence: OT DMZ firewall rule base; data flow diagram v3

implementation_statement: Recipe authors cannot approve their own recipes; control logic changes are prepared by one engineer and approved by the Controls Engineering Manager through MOC; SIS changes need a second engineer and the Process Safety Manager.
evidence: Batch system role matrix; MOC approvals

implementation_statement: Operator roles cannot change control logic or alarm limits outside a defined band. Engineer and administrator rights are held by 22 controls engineers and I&E technicians and reviewed quarterly. IT privileged access to OT DMZ servers goes through PAM.
evidence: Quarterly OT privileged review 2026-Q2; PAM report

implementation_statement: Gateway and OT DMZ accounts lock after 5 failed attempts. DCS operator consoles do not lock out, by design, so that an operator is never locked out during an upset; failed logons are logged and alerted instead (documented exception EXC-OT-003).
Gateway sessions and EWS logons display the approved system use notice. Operator HMI screens display a short notice on the login banner.
Engineering accounts are limited to one concurrent session on the DCS engineering server; gateway sessions are limited to one per account.
EWS and OT DMZ servers lock after 15 minutes. Operator stations stay unlocked for continuous process view, protected by control room access control (documented exception EXC-OT-004).
Gateway sessions end after 8 hours or 30 minutes idle; engineering sessions on the DCS end at logoff or after 60 minutes idle.

control_name: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication
implementation_statement: Operator stations display process graphics in view-only mode without authentication; no control action is possible without logon.

All remote access to PLT-01 OT goes through the central remote access gateway in the OT DMZ: named accounts, MFA, per-session approval by the shift supervisor, session recording, and access only to approved targets. No other remote path exists at PLT-01 (verified by firewall review 2026-08-12).
evidence: Gateway policy; session approvals; P07 AC-17 results
regulatory_driver: C-CHEMICAL-R02 (101.650(a)(4)); C-CHEMICAL-R02 (101.650(e)(3)(v)); C-CHEMICAL-R02 (101.650(f)(3)); C-CHEMICAL-R01 (27.230(a)(8), voluntary benchmark)

implementation_statement: The gateway records every session and sends session events to the SIEM; the SOC reviews unapproved or out-of-window sessions.
evidence: Session recordings; SIEM use case OT-RA-01

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions use TLS from the user to the gateway and encrypted protocols from the gateway to jump hosts.
The gateway is the single managed access control point for remote access to OT at the 11 plants it serves, including PLT-01.
Privileged remote commands (logic download, SIS access) are not permitted remotely; they require an on-site engineer. Remote integrator sessions are view and configure only, with on-site download.
No wireless in the control or safety networks. Plant wireless for tablets is on the business network. Monthly wireless surveys at PLT-01 look for rogue access points near control rooms.
Mobile devices cannot connect to OT. Integrator laptops are not allowed on the control network; integrators use company-provided EWS or the gateway.
External systems (integrator laptops, customer systems) may not connect to OT. Toll customers receive batch records through the SL-2 portal, not from OT.
Customer-owned recipes are shared only under toll agreements; the toll account team decides what batch data each customer receives.
evidence: Toll agreement template; SL-2 portal role design

implementation_statement: Not applicable: the GC-PCBMS hosts no publicly accessible content (tailored out under SP 800-53B).
POL-01 and STD-01.4 (training) set awareness and role-based training for IT and OT, including MTSA cybersecurity training at PLT-01.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Enterprise awareness training is annual with phishing simulations. PLT-01 adds the MTSA topics in 101.650(d)(1)(ii)-(v). 94% of PLT-01 personnel completed it by 2026-01-12; 212 contractor personnel did not and are escorted or monitored by trained staff under 101.650(d)(3) until they complete it (POAM-007).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Role-based OT security training for operators, controls engineers, and I&E technicians; key personnel training under 101.650(d)(2) was completed by 2026-01-12. DOT in-depth security training covers loading staff (49 CFR 172.704(a)(5)).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Training records are kept in the learning system for at least 2 years for MTSA purposes (33 CFR 105.225(b)(1)) and 5 years for enterprise purposes.
POL-01 and STD-01.6 (logging and monitoring) apply to OT; STD-01.6 lists the OT event sources.

Logged events: DCS logons, role changes, control logic downloads, alarm limit and setpoint changes outside the operator band, recipe approvals, SIS mode and keyswitch changes, gateway sessions, OT DMZ server security events, and firewall denies.
evidence: STD-01.6 event list; DCS audit configuration

implementation_statement: DCS audit records include time, user, station, tag, old value, and new value.
The DCS audit server keeps 180 days locally; the historian and log collector in the OT DMZ have capacity alerts.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: Log collector failures alert the SOC within 15 minutes.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews OT alerts 24x7 with OT monitoring analysts; the CySO reviews PLT-01 OT reports weekly. Gap: no SIEM use case alerts on alarm limit changes on safety-relevant tags or on SIS keyswitch position changes, which would have caught the P08 scenario early (POAM-022).
evidence: SOC runbooks; SIEM use case list; P07 AU-6 results

control_name: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
implementation_statement: The SIEM provides search and reporting over OT logs forwarded from PLT-01.
OT time comes from two GPS-disciplined time servers in the PLT-01 control network, which also serve the OT DMZ.
OT logs are forwarded to the SIEM, where only SOC administrators can change retention; local DCS audit files are read-only to non-administrators.
Named DCS and gateway accounts tie each control change to a person; shared integrator accounts are a gap tracked under AC-2.
OT logs are retained 1 year online and 2 years in archive (meets 33 CFR 105.225 records retention for cyber incident records).
Audit generation is enabled on all DCS servers, EWS, OT DMZ servers, the gateway, and the IT/OT firewalls.
POL-01 and STD-01.8 (assessment and authorization) cover OT systems.

Internal Audit assesses the GC-PCBMS annually (P07, 2026-07-13 to 2026-08-28). The assessors have no assigned cybersecurity duties at PLT-01, which also meets the independence test for MTSA Cybersecurity Plan audits (101.630(f)(4)).
Interconnections (ERP order relay, historian replication, SL-2 portal batch record export, terminal automation link to tank gauging) are documented in interconnection records (section 8).
Weaknesses are tracked in the P07 POA&M in the GRC platform with owners and dates; the CySO also keeps the MTSA list of unresolved vulnerabilities (101.630(c)(12)).
The Chief Operating Officer is the authorizing official equivalent and made the operate-with-conditions decision on 2026-09-08 (section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring: weekly OT metrics (open KEVs, unapproved changes, remote sessions, backup status) to the Director of OT Security, quarterly to the CISO and the executive risk committee.

An OT penetration test of PLT-01 is scheduled for 2027-Q1, before the Cybersecurity Plan submission, as 101.650(e)(2) requires in conjunction with plan renewal; earlier tests covered the OT DMZ only (2025).
evidence: Test scope 2027-Q1; 2025 OT DMZ test report

implementation_statement: Internal connections between the control network, SIS networks, and terminal PLC network are documented and limited by the PLT-01 zone firewalls.
POL-01 and STD-01.3 (configuration management) apply to OT; OT changes use the MOC system.

Baselines exist for DCS servers, EWS, operator stations, and OT DMZ servers. Gap: the MTSA approved hardware, firmware, and software list is incomplete for the terminal PLCs and tank gauging (POAM-006).
Control logic, alarm limit, recipe, and SIS changes require MOC and, for SIS, a pre-startup review. Gap: 7 of 40 sampled DCS changes had no MOC record (POAM-001).
evidence: MOC records; DCS change log; P07 CM-3 results

control_name: Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes
implementation_statement: Planned: automated comparison of DCS configuration against the approved baseline, with alerts for unauthorized changes, as part of POAM-001 (2027-03-31).

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: Control logic changes are tested on the PLT-01 simulator before download; SIS changes are tested and validated per the proof-test procedure before return to service.
Security impact is a required MOC question for any OT change; PHA revalidations include control system compromise scenarios for the ammonia unit (2025).
evidence: MOC form v7; 2025 ammonia unit PHA

implementation_statement: Only engineer and administrator roles can change logic; SIS keys are held by the Controls Engineering Manager; download requires on-site presence.
evidence: DCS role matrix; SIS key log

control_name: Automated Access Enforcement and Audit Records
implementation_statement: The DCS enforces role-based change rights and records every change in its audit trail.
Hardening settings from the OT Center of Excellence baseline (STD-01.3 annex B) apply to OT Windows hosts; deviations are recorded as exceptions.

Unused services and ports are disabled; application allowlisting runs on all DCS servers, EWS, and 29 of 38 operator stations. Gap: 9 legacy operator stations in Blend Hall 1 cannot run the allowlisting agent (POAM-020).
Allow-by-exception software policy enforced through allowlisting where supported (see CM-7).

OT asset inventory from passive monitoring plus engineering records, with critical IT and OT systems designated. Gap: network map and device configuration records for the terminal and truck rack PLC networks are incomplete (POAM-006).
evidence: OT asset inventory; network map v2

implementation_statement: Passive OT monitoring detects new devices on the PLT-01 control and supervisory networks and alerts the SOC.
PLT-01 OT configuration management plan v3 defines roles, configuration items, and the link to MOC.
Software licenses for DCS, batch, historian, and SIS tools are tracked by the DCS vendor support agreement and procurement.
Users cannot install software on OT hosts; only administrators install software from the OT patch and media staging service.
The location of SSI, recipes, and process safety information in OT is recorded in the OT data inventory.
POL-01 and STD-01.7 (contingency) cover OT; the OT contingency plan template comes from the OT Center of Excellence.

The PLT-01 OT contingency plan sets recovery order and safe states from the BIA (P05 BP-01 to BP-04). Gap: detailed restore procedures exist for the ammonia unit area only; the Chlor Unit and blend hall areas are due with POAM-003.
The OT contingency plan is coordinated with the RMP emergency response program, the MTSA Facility Security Plan, and the enterprise IT disaster recovery plan.
Controls engineers and shift supervisors train annually on OT recovery and safe-state procedures.

The OT contingency plan is exercised annually. Gap: restore from the OT backup vault has been tested for 1 of 3 DCS areas (ammonia area, 2026-03); the Chlor Unit and blend hall areas have never been restore-tested (POAM-003).
evidence: Restore test report 2026-03; P07 CP-4 results

implementation_statement: OT backups are copied to the OT backup vault at DC-1 with a second copy at DC-2.
Not applicable as written: a chemical process cannot move to an alternate processing site. The equivalent is volume transfer to PLT-03 and PLT-06 for common products (P05 BP-01).
Emergency communications at PLT-01 do not depend on the business network: cellular phones, printed call lists, radios to the gate and fire brigade, and the mass notification service.
evidence: Emergency kit inventory; monthly radio checks

implementation_statement: Daily backups of DCS configuration, batch database, historian configuration, and SIS programs (after each approved change) go to the OT backup vault with offline and immutable copies. Gap: toll customer recipes are backed up only as part of the batch database, with no separate recipe vault or integrity check (POAM-016).
Backup jobs verify checksums; quarterly sample restores to a test host.
Approved SIS programs and DCS logic are stored separately in the vault from routine backups.
Recovery procedures rebuild DCS servers and EWS from vault images and reload approved logic. Only the ammonia area recovery is proven (12 h RTO met in 2026-03 test).
Restore within 12 hours per DCS area is the target; proven for 1 of 3 areas (POAM-003).
POL-02 and STD-02.2 (authentication) apply to OT, with OT exceptions recorded.
Individual accounts for operators, engineers, and remote users. Local panel HMIs at the truck rack and terminal use role logons, with compensating physical controls (exception EXC-OT-011).

MFA for all privileged IT access to OT DMZ servers and for all remote OT access. Local console logon to DCS engineering stations is protected by control room access control (OT tailoring, exception EXC-OT-002).

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: MFA for all non-privileged remote access through the gateway.
Passive monitoring identifies devices by MAC and protocol fingerprint; switch port security on control network switches.
OT identifiers are unique and never reused; integrator accounts carry the company name and person.

Password length and complexity enforced where the device allows. Gap: P07 testing found default vendor passwords on the terminal tank gauging server web interface and two truck rack PLC web interfaces (POAM-013).
Passwords are masked on all OT consoles and the gateway.
Cryptographic modules in the gateway and OT DMZ servers use validated libraries; controllers do not perform authentication cryptography.
Integrators and vendors authenticate as named non-organizational users on the gateway with MFA, sponsored by a PLT-01 engineer.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Gateway sessions require re-authentication after 8 hours or on role change.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Identity proofing at hire by HR; integrator staff are proofed by the integrator under contract and verified at badge issue.
POL-03 and STD-03.1 to STD-03.3 cover OT incidents, with the PLT-01 Cyber Incident Response Plan as an annex to the MTSA Cybersecurity Plan.
Annual incident response training for the SOC, OT engineers, and shift supervisors.
Two cybersecurity drills a year at PLT-01 and one annual exercise, combined with MTSA security drills where possible; the 2026-03-19 tabletop covered an OT ransomware scenario with the MSSP.
The SOC handles OT incidents with OT runbooks; the PLT-01 Plant Manager is incident commander for process safety; safe state comes before forensics (P08).
Incidents are tracked in the SOC case system, and MTSA cyber incidents also in the FSO records (33 CFR 105.225(b)(3)).

Reporting duties are in the P08 notification matrix: immediate reports under 33 CFR 6.16-1 to the FBI, CISA, and the Captain of the Port; release reports to the NRC; SEC 8-K through the disclosure committee.
The SOC, the MSSP OT practice, and the DCS vendor emergency service support incident handling.

The enterprise IR plan and the PLT-01 Cyber Incident Response Plan exist. Gap: the materiality playbook covers data breaches only, and the disclosure committee has no operations member and has never exercised an OT scenario (POAM-004).
evidence: IR plan v5; disclosure committee charter

responsible_role: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS
implementation_statement: Maintenance of OT follows the mechanical integrity program and STD-01.3 for software maintenance.
SIS proof tests and DCS maintenance are scheduled in the maintenance system; proof tests are on schedule for both SIS.
Maintenance tools and laptops for OT are company-owned, scanned at the media station, and kept in the engineering office.
Nonlocal maintenance only through the gateway with approval and recording (see AC-17).
Integrator staff on site are escorted unless trained and badged; maintenance personnel lists are kept by the Controls Engineering Manager.
Critical spares (controllers, power supplies, I/O cards, server images) are kept on site under the DCS vendor agreement.
POL-04 and STD-04.2 (media) apply to OT.
Removable media for OT are company-issued and stored in the engineering office.
OT media are labeled SSI or Restricted as applicable (49 CFR Part 1520; POL-04).
OT media and backup drives are stored in locked cabinets in the engineering office.
Media leaving the site are encrypted and logged.
OT drives are sanitized per NIST SP 800-88 before disposal.
USB ports are disabled on operator stations; media must be scanned at the kiosk before use on EWS. Gap: 4 of 6 EWS accepted an unscanned test USB device (POAM-021).
Corporate security policy and the MTSA Facility Security Plan govern PLT-01 physical access.
Authorized lists for control rooms, rack rooms, and SIS cabinets are kept by the FSO and reviewed quarterly.
Badge and TWIC readers control PLT-01 entry and the marine terminal secure area; control rooms and rack rooms need a second badge; SIS cabinets are locked.
Network cabling for the control network runs in locked trays and rack rooms.
Operator station screens face away from windows; control rooms are restricted areas.
Video and badge logs cover control rooms and rack rooms; the FSO reviews exceptions weekly.
Visitor logs are kept for 2 years.
Power cabling to DCS and SIS cabinets is protected in dedicated trays.
Emergency shutdown buttons for each unit are in the control room and at field stations, protected from accidental activation.
UPS on DCS, SIS, and control rooms; generators with a 72-hour fuel contract.
Emergency lighting in control rooms and rack rooms, tested monthly.
Fire detection and suppression in control and rack rooms; the plant fire brigade responds.
Rack rooms are climate controlled and alarmed.
Rack rooms are above flood level and have water sensors.
Deliveries to the control building are inspected at the gate.
Not applicable: no alternate work site for OT; remote work on OT is limited to gateway sessions.
Control rooms are in a blast-resistant building away from the ammonia unit and Chlor Unit.
POL-01 sets planning duties; this SSP follows NIST SP 800-18 Rev. 2.

This SSP is approved. Gap: the MTSA Cybersecurity Plan (101.630) and Cybersecurity Assessment (101.650(e)(1)) for PLT-01 are in progress and due to the Coast Guard by 2027-07-16; internal target 2027-03-31 (POAM-008).
evidence: SSP v1.0; Cybersecurity Plan draft outline

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Rules of behavior (POL-05) are acknowledged at hire and annually; integrators sign them before gateway access.
The OT reference architecture (zones and conduits, OT DMZ, one-way paths) follows NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3.
High baseline selected with OT tailoring (section 6).
Tailoring decisions and exceptions are recorded in section 6 and the exception register.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: HR policy and STD-01.5 (personnel security) apply.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Positions with OT engineering, SIS, or terminal access are designated sensitive.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Background checks for sensitive positions; TWIC for unescorted access to the marine terminal secure area; legacy CFATS personnel surety measures kept.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: HR leaver events trigger badge, IT, and gateway removal automatically; OT directory accounts are removed by ticket. Gap: 3 of 25 sampled leavers still had enabled DCS accounts (POAM-023).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Transfers trigger an access review by the receiving manager.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Confidentiality and acceptable use agreements at hire and annually.
Integrator contracts require background checks, training, and prompt notice of staff departures (except 2 legacy contracts, see SR-6).

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Sanctions process for policy violations.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: Position descriptions for OT roles include security duties.
POL-01 and the enterprise risk method (P01) apply to OT.
The GC-PCBMS is categorized in section 6 of this SSP.

Enterprise risk analysis (P01) and the PHA program cover the GC-PCBMS. Gap: control system compromise scenarios are in the ammonia unit PHA (2025) but not yet in the Chlor Unit PHA (revalidation 2027), and the MTSA Cybersecurity Assessment is not done (POAM-008).

Passive OT vulnerability identification and quarterly authenticated scans of OT DMZ hosts; the CISA KEV catalog is matched daily. Gap: 37 KEV findings on PLT-01 OT assets were older than 30 days without documented compensating controls (see SI-2, POAM-002).
Risk responses are recorded in P01 and the POA&M.
Criticality analysis: the SIS, DCS controllers, and terminal emergency shutdown are designated critical OT systems.
Acquisition policy requires security requirements for OT purchases.
OT security is funded through the OT Center of Excellence budget and plant capital plans.
OT projects follow the engineering lifecycle with security gates at design, FAT, and SAT.
New OT contracts include security requirements and vendor notification duties. Gap: the DCS vendor support contract and 2 integrator contracts lack them (POAM-010).
Vendor documentation for DCS, SIS, and PLCs is kept in the engineering document system.
Security engineering principles (defense in depth, least functionality, SIS independence) are in the OT reference architecture.
External services: the MSSP OT practice, the DCS vendor remote support, and Cloud provider A for historian replicas. Gap: see SA-4.
Integrators make changes under company MOC and configuration control.
Integrator changes are tested on the simulator and at SAT before download.
DCS and SIS vendors are evaluated for secure development practices at selection.
DCS vendor training for engineers is part of the support agreement.

control_name: Developer Security and Privacy Architecture and Design
implementation_statement: Vendor security architecture documentation is reviewed at selection and upgrade.
Integrator staff with OT access are screened under contract (see PS-7).
9 operator stations in Blend Hall 1 run an unsupported operating system until the 2027 DCS console upgrade; compensating controls are network isolation and monitoring (POAM-020).
POL-01 and STD-01.2 (network and communications) apply.

control_name: Separation of System and User Functionality
implementation_statement: User functions (operator HMIs) are separated from system management (engineering and administration servers).
SIS logic solvers are separate from the DCS and connect only through a read-only interface for status.
Shared resources on DCS servers are not shared across security roles.
IT/OT firewalls rate-limit traffic into the OT DMZ; the control network has no internet path.
PLT-01 has an OT DMZ between business and control networks and zone firewalls for SIS and terminal networks. Gap: 14 of 212 OT DMZ firewall rules were broader than documented or unused (POAM-012).

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default between all OT zones.
SIS networks are isolated from the control network except for the read-only status interface.

Traffic between the OT DMZ and enterprise is encrypted. Control network protocols between controllers and stations are not encrypted because the controllers do not support it; segmentation and monitoring compensate (documented under 101.650(c)(2) "when technically feasible").
OT DMZ sessions end after 30 minutes idle.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-06 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Keys for OT DMZ certificates and the gateway are managed by the enterprise key service.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-06 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Approved cryptography for remote access and replication.
Not applicable: no collaborative computing devices (cameras, microphones) in OT hosts.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-06 Cloud landing zone (Cloud provider A)
implementation_statement: Certificates for OT DMZ services come from the enterprise PKI.
Mobile code is blocked on OT hosts through allowlisting.
Enterprise DNS provides signed responses for OT DMZ names.

control_name: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)
implementation_statement: OT DMZ resolvers validate responses.

control_name: Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service
implementation_statement: DNS for the OT DMZ is redundant; the control network does not use DNS.
Gateway sessions are authenticated end to end.
On loss of communication or power, controllers and the SIS go to defined safe states (valves fail closed, pumps stop), per the safety requirements specification.
OT backups in the vault are encrypted; DCS servers hold recipes and SSI on encrypted volumes where supported.
Operating systems on OT hosts provide process isolation.
POL-01 and STD-01.6 cover OT integrity and monitoring.

OT patches are qualified by the DCS vendor and applied at planned outages through the patch staging service. Gap: 37 KEV findings on PLT-01 OT assets were older than 30 days without documented compensating controls; the MTSA rule requires patching or documented compensating controls "without delay" (POAM-002).
Allowlisting on OT hosts where supported; malware scanning at the media kiosk and in the OT DMZ; EDR on OT DMZ servers.

Passive OT monitoring on the PLT-01 control and supervisory networks with alerts to the SOC. Gap: the terminal and truck rack PLC networks are not monitored; enterprise-wide, OT logs from 5 plants do not reach the SIEM (POAM-011).
Traffic through the IT/OT boundary and the OT DMZ is monitored for unusual flows.
The SOC receives CISA ICS advisories, vendor bulletins, and sector ISAC alerts and routes OT items to the CySO.
SIS proof tests verify safety functions on schedule.

Approved SIS programs and DCS logic are stored in the vault. Gap: comparison of running SIS programs with the approved copies is manual and irregular (last done 2025-11 for the Chlor Unit SIS) (POAM-009).
Planned: monthly automated comparison of running SIS and DCS logic with approved copies (POAM-009, 2027-01-31).
Email filtering on the enterprise; no email in OT.
Batch system validates recipe parameters against engineering limits; operator entries outside limits are rejected.
Error messages on HMIs do not expose system details.
Process safety records and batch records are retained per the PSM, RMP, and toll agreement retention rules.
Operating system memory protections are enabled on OT hosts.
Supply chain risk management policy and STD-01.9 apply to OT.
The enterprise SCRM plan covers DCS, SIS, PLC, and integrator suppliers.
Supply chain controls for OT purchases (approved vendors, verified sources). Gap: see SR-6.
OT components are bought from the vendor or authorized distributors only.

Tier-1 OT suppliers are assessed every two years. Gap: 2 of 6 DCS and PLC integrators have no security clauses and the DCS vendor support contract lacks a vulnerability and incident notification clause required by 101.650(f)(2) (POAM-010).
Notification agreements with suppliers are being added at contract renewal (see SR-6).
Tamper-evident packaging is checked on receipt of controllers and SIS cards.
New controllers and SIS components are inspected and firmware verified before installation.
Spares come from authorized channels; counterfeit concerns are reported to the vendor.
Retired OT components are sanitized and disposed of under MP-6.
